title: The curve adapter uses a fixed supply for fees.
code_smells: The adapter selects ordinary curve fees with fixed supply; synthetic fees use live supply; the parser accepts multiple fee tiers.
path: A future pump fee schedule contains multiple tiers → a token holder burns tokens → pricing_inputs selects ordinary fees using 10^15 supply → q <= rT quotes and fee gates use a different tier from the venue's live-supply tier.
proof: This is a conditional arithmetic example, not a verified current venue configuration. Set vt = 536,500,000,000,000 raw tokens, vq = 60,000,000,000 lamports, live supply = 900,000,000,000,000, and q = 1,000,000,000,000 <= rT. A two-tier schedule with protocol fee 200 bps below 105,000,000,000 lamports and 100 bps at or above it gives fixed-supply market cap floor(vq * 10^15 / vt) = 111,835,973,904, but live-supply market cap = 100,652,376,514. Ordinary short.win quotes select 100 bps: ceil(q*vq/(vt-q))+1 = 112,044,819; total = 113,165,268. The curve charge formula documented in sol_leg.rs with 200 bps gives floor(q*vq/(vt-q))+1 = 112,044,818; total = 114,285,715, or 1,120,447 lamports above the quote. All products fit u128. pricing_inputs already receives live supply, but uses it only for synthetic_fees. read_state's executable predicate does not constrain the schedule to one tier.
description: The curve adapter selects the wrong fee after burns if pump adds tiers; this review does not verify such a current schedule.
fix: Use live mint supply for ordinary curve fees and the fee at the EMA price.
unverified: fees.rs:45-50 explicitly says the deployed curve schedule has only threshold 0; no live multi-tier schedule or unprivileged schedule change was verified. This is a future-configuration hardening lead, not a present exploit finding.

related_locations: crates/shortwin-math/src/pool.rs:598; crates/shortwin-math/src/pool.rs:1459; crates/shortwin-math/src/pool.rs:1474; crates/shortwin-math/src/pool.rs:1487; crates/shortwin-math/src/pool.rs:1660
title: Repeated sync calls discard fractional lender credits.
code_smells: An unsigned owner account reaches touch_pot; a current lender's touch floors each accrual and resets both snapshots without a lender remainder.
path: Public market accrual increases acc → an outsider calls sync_lender(0) for a current lender → touch_pot reaches touch_tail → floor(shares * (acc-snap) / WAD) credits zero → snap advances → later calls cannot recover that fraction.
proof: Pure integer accounting trace: WAD = 10^18, total_shares = 3,000, lender shares = 1,000, initial acc = carry = pending = snap = 0. Three market credits of one lamport produce acc increments [333,333,333,333,333; 333,333,333,333,333; 333,333,333,333,334] with carried remainders [1,000; 2,000; 0]. A sync after each increment adds floor(1,000 * increment / 10^18) = 0, leaving pending = 0. One touch after all three instead adds floor(1,000 * 1,000,000,000,000,000 / 10^18) = 1 lamport. The same quotient structure applies to real through acc_r. sync_lender.rs:118-126 permits the non-owner path; lines 134-137 persist the resulting lender state. No share-epoch conversion is needed.
description: An outsider repeatedly removes fractional lender credits; material harm beyond the protocol's stated downward rounding remains unverified.
fix: Carry each lender's fractional accrual across touches and share changes.
unverified: pool.rs explicitly specifies downward rounding of SOL credits. Each extra touch removes less than one lamport. This review did not establish profitable extraction, material aggregate harm, or an accepted-state transaction sequence with substantial loss. Preserve this trail for the economic and invariant reviews; do not promote it solely from the three-credit example.

LEAD | program: shortwin | function: close_short | bug_class: hardening-position-status-unchecked | group_key: shortwin | close_short | hardening-position-status-unchecked
title: Exit instructions omit the position status check
file: programs/shortwin/src/instructions/close_short.rs:82
related_locations: programs/shortwin/src/instructions/liquidate.rs:123; programs/shortwin/src/instructions/expire.rs:93; programs/shortwin/src/instructions/sol_settle.rs:122; programs/shortwin/src/instructions/add_margin.rs:63; programs/shortwin/src/state/position.rs:18
code_smells: AddMargin requires position.status == POSITION_OPEN, but CloseShort, Liquidate, Expire, and SolSettle do not.
description: A future instruction that sets POSITION_EXIT_IN_PROGRESS can leave its position eligible for close_short and keeper exits because those paths omit status checks.
limits: This is not an exploit in the reviewed build. POSITION_EXIT_IN_PROGRESS is reserved for v1.1, and open_short currently writes only POSITION_OPEN. The independent gate already exists in add_margin; the other four Accounts structs check the account's borrower, market, and PDA but not its status. A future non-open state must be excluded explicitly before this omission becomes reachable.
fix: Add the POSITION_OPEN constraint to each exit instruction before any instruction writes another live position status.

location: services/keeper/src/view.rs:263; services/keeper/src/view.rs:284; keeper::load_with_positions
title: The keeper loads account layouts without their version checks.
code_smells: decode_zc checks the owner, discriminator, and minimum byte length; load_with_positions accepts GlobalConfig and Market without a version check.
description: The keeper interprets a future account layout with its old types if an upgrade preserves the discriminator and minimum size.
proof: view.rs:48-55 uses pod_read_unaligned after the owner/discriminator/size checks. load_with_positions:263-267 accepts GlobalConfig, and its market loop accepts decoded Market data before venue_kind; neither compares CONFIG_VERSION or MARKET_VERSION. The on-chain open_short Accounts constraints require both versions. A stored version byte different from the expected version therefore reaches keeper projection while the on-chain instruction refuses it. No currently reachable unauthorized state write or direct fund loss was proved.
fix: Check each decoded config and market version before the keeper uses its fields.

title: A temporary withdrawal changes the live settlement legs.
code_smells: The settlement input uses live venue reserves for b_live and sigma_live, while only the CR gate uses the EMA liquidity floor.
description: An LP can force SOL settlement after a temporary withdrawal; the current borrower loss and profitability still need an independent numerical trace.
path: LP withdraws unlocked venue liquidity -> sol_settle reads the reduced live reserves -> LP restores liquidity in the same transaction; repeat across the required observation updates.
proof: inputs:208 reads state.liquidity(); inputs:213-216 computes quotes.live(state.x, state.y); inputs:223 applies bounds::spot_liquidity only to the CR quote; SettleInputs carries the original l_live, b_live, and sigma_live. The module comment at arming.rs:40-52 states that AIR-20 remains reachable when the honest state lies outside the box, and identifies a 20% pool_lock_min_bps / 1% fee case. That prior disclosure is context, not a guard. This pass traced the adapter/transaction boundary but did not independently reconstruct current box corners, arming state, borrower payout, and attacker financing with concrete numbers. No finding is asserted from that comment alone.
fix: Require a live settlement leg that a temporary liquidity withdrawal cannot create.

FINDING | program: shortwin-math | function: withdraw_in | bug_class: carry-crosses-empty-pool | group_key: shortwin-math | withdraw_in | carry-crosses-empty-pool
location: crates/shortwin-math/src/pool.rs:1908 (shortwin-math::withdraw_in)
title: The last withdrawal leaves SOL carry for the next lender
confidence: 97
root_cause: withdraw_in leaves carry and carry_r intact when total_shares reaches zero, so a later cohort receives the previous cohort's undistributed SOL.
invariant: A new lender must not acquire the old cohort's accrued or realised SOL after every old share has been withdrawn.
violation_path: Old lender deposits -> unrelated income enters through sweep_trader -> old lender withdraws all shares and receives zero SOL -> sweep_trader clears the required source bit -> attacker deposits one raw token -> attacker donates one lamport and calls sweep_trader -> attacker withdraws all shares and receives the old income plus that lamport.
path: Use a live, list-only market with an accepted ordinary SPL mint, no borrowed tokens, deposit_hold_until = -1, and initially empty lender accounting. The old owner signs its deposit and withdrawal. The attacker signs only its own deposit, one-lamport System transfer, and withdrawal; sweep_trader requires no authority signature. Pass the genuine market, vaults, mint, token program, trader and trader_wsol accounts. Neither owner needs share-epoch records. The attacker's withdrawal passes min_tokens = 1 and min_sol = 1000 in the first example.
proof: All arithmetic below uses the frozen production source; no build, test, or executable PoC was run.
  1. Let WAD = 10^18, VA = 1, VS = 1000. The old lender deposits A = 10^18 raw tokens. shares_for_tokens returns A*1000 = 10^21 shares. Thus T=A, B=0, S=10^21, acc=acc_r=carry=carry_r=0.
  2. An unrelated income payer sends X=999 lamports to the market's trader. sweep_trader normalises those actual lamports into MarketVault and calls pool::sweep (instructions/sweep_trader.rs:279 onward; pool.rs:2200 onward). lender_sol=999 and vest_bal=999. This uses actual deposited SOL, not a fabricated counter. There is no minimum sweep amount. The transfer and sweep can share one transaction so the trader ends with zero lamports.
  3. Before the vest ends, the old lender withdraws all S shares. tokens_for_shares returns floor((1000*A)*(A+1)/(1000*A+1000))=A. B=0, so the production LastSharesBorrowed guard passes. withdraw_in flushes the 999-lamport vest at pool.rs:1897-1904. credit_pos computes floor(999*10^18/10^21)=0 and carry=999*10^18; credit_r_in computes the same zero delta and carry_r=999*10^18. The old lender's pending and real both remain zero. The function sets S=0 and clears only wipe_swept, at lines 1906-1912. Both carries remain.
  4. The production withdraw handler immediately calls pool::claim (instructions/withdraw.rs:212-215). It pays zero because pending=real=claimed=0. pool::closable is true: no shares, no pending, no lock, and current epoch. The handler closes the lender account. A claim before this withdrawal also pays zero because both index deltas are zero. A claim after the close cannot recover the 999 lamports. Setting min_sol=999 only makes the old withdrawal fail; it does not expose a path that claims the carry.
  5. The attacker calls a zero sweep. For the list-only venue only the trader source bit is required. No SOL moves, no live wipe record exists, and the carry remains. The attacker deposits one raw token, which mints 1000 shares against T=B=S=0. Its initial snapshots are acc=acc_r=0. The existing lender_sol remains 999.
  6. The attacker transfers one actual lamport to trader and calls sweep_trader. The trader bit is already set, so the new lamport vests normally: lender_sol=1000, vest_bal=1. It then withdraws all its 1000 shares before the new vest ends. Its full exit flushes the one lamport. Both index numerators equal 1*WAD + 999*WAD = 1000*WAD. Division by S=1000 gives delta=WAD. The lender touch credits pending=real=1000, and both carries become zero. pool::claim pays all 1000 lamports. Its raw token also returns in full. Its net SOL receipt before transaction fees is the old owner's 999 lamports.
  7. The pot is zero throughout: unmatched=0, and no pot draw is required. This is cross-cohort index allocation, not recovery of a stranded pot. MarketVault's actual lamports always equal its rent plus the tracked SOL, so its rent-floor and backing checks do not reject the path.
production_bounds: deposit accepts amount:u64 and checks amount>0, minted>0, min_shares, arithmetic, mint safety, and pool conditions; it imposes no smaller token amount cap. The initial A=10^18 is below u64::MAX. mint_filter::check_mint_safety (programs/shortwin/src/mint_filter.rs:64-100) does not cap mint supply or decimals. An initialized non-native SPL mint with no freeze authority and supply at least A suffices. A list-only market permits deposits, withdrawals and trader sweeps, so open caps and min_notional do not participate. For a larger fully traced instance, A=18,000,000,000,000,000,000 also fits u64, S=18,000,000,000,000,000,000,000, and X=17,999 satisfies X*WAD<S. The same path pays the next lender 18,000 lamports after its one-lamport donation, a 17,999-lamport cross-cohort transfer before fees. The initial-deposit case has X < 1000*A/WAD, so at the u64 token limit this specific construction transfers at most 18,446 whole lamports per empty-pool transition. Higher share/token ratios can increase the representation quantum, but this report does not assert their maximum reachability or profit.
intent_check: pool.rs documents global carry as an undistributed remainder in [0,S), and explicitly drops carries into dust when an epoch rolls (maybe_roll_in). Its last-withdraw documentation says the last lender receives the unreleased vest. The zero-share withdrawal branch neither pays nor drops the carries. No read source states that the next depositor owns the previous cohort's carry. This is larger than one-lamport rounding dust, but its bounded magnitude remains relevant to final triage.
description: A new lender takes the previous lender's SOL because the last withdrawal leaves both index carries in the empty pool.
fix: Pay whole-lamport carry to the last lender and clear both carries before the next deposit.
minimal_diff: This proposed diff pays whole units to the last holder and drops only sub-lamport residues, with the existing checked helpers; it is untested.
```diff
--- a/crates/shortwin-math/src/pool.rs
+++ b/crates/shortwin-math/src/pool.rs
@@ -1906,6 +1906,15 @@ fn withdraw_in(
     l.shares = sub_u128(l.shares, shares)?;
     p.total_shares = sub_u128(p.total_shares, shares)?;
     if p.total_shares == 0 {
+        l.pending = to_i64(add_i128(i128::from(l.pending), p.carry / WAD_I)?)?;
+        l.real = add_u64(l.real, to_u64(p.carry_r / WAD)?)?;
+        p.dust = add_i128(
+            add_i128(p.dust, p.carry % WAD_I)?,
+            to_i128(p.carry_r % WAD)?,
+        )?;
+        p.carry = 0;
+        p.carry_r = 0;
+
         // AIR-08: the market has no lender again; SOL that reaches the trader from now on is
         // the protocol's (KI-10), so the next deposit waits for the sweeps, as after a wipe.
         p.wipe_swept = 0;
```

LEAD | program: shortwin | function: deposit | bug_class: donation-extends-deposit-hold | group_key: shortwin | deposit | donation-extends-deposit-hold
location: programs/shortwin/src/instructions/deposit.rs:130-135; crates/shortwin-math/src/pool.rs:965-986
program_function: shortwin::deposit
title: Small donations keep a settlement hold active
code_smells: The deposit hold requires an empty shared vest; any caller adds a new vest through a trader sweep.
description: An attacker extends a deposit hold with one-lamport sweeps; a safe fix must preserve the protection for historical rewards and split claims.
invariant: A hold that protects a completed settlement should eventually permit deposits despite unrelated later donations.
partial_path: A settlement leaves S>0 and a vest without a dust flush; sol_settle.rs:327-328 arms deposit_hold_until. An attacker sends a one-lamport System transfer to trader, followed by sweep_trader before each vest expiry. The public sweep adds to the same vest that deposit requires to reach zero.
concrete_trace: Let a held vest contain 1,000,000 lamports and span 21,600 seconds, with both source bits already set and no other income or withdrawals. At t=end-1, the prologue releases floor(1,000,000*21,599/21,600)=999,953, leaving 47. A one-lamport sweep computes floor((47*1+1*21,600)/(47+1))=450, so vest_bal=48 and the new end is t+450. At the new end minus one second, release leaves ceil(48/450)=1. Another one-lamport sweep gives vest_bal=2 and a new end t+floor((1+21,600)/2)=t+10,800. Each later sweep at end-1 leaves one old lamport and adds one new lamport, so the 10,800-second cycle repeats. No sweep races a completed vest; each can occur before expiry while deposits already fail. Costs are one lamport and transaction fees per cycle. The instruction contains no signer, minimum amount, or cooldown that prevents it.
related_path: Once the original vest has fully released, an attacker can also sweep a fresh one-lamport donation before the first successful deposit. Only deposit clears deposit_hold_until to -1. The fresh vest then blocks that deposit for another lump_vest_s; this variant requires transaction ordering at reopening.
recoveries_and_limits: Withdrawals, claims and position exits remain available. The last lender can flush the vest through a full withdrawal when no tokens remain borrowed. A full wipe also flushes it. A successful deposit during an unprotected gap clears the hold. The trace does not prove a theft or a permanent block after the attacker stops. The specific 1,000,000-lamport starting vest is a valid pool state; a full production settlement transaction that produces that exact state was not constructed.
intent_and_open_question: Market.deposit_hold_until and deposit.rs expressly state that later credits can extend the shared vest, so this lead preserves that stated design rather than treating extension alone as a defect. The low-cost recurrent donation path needs an explicit liveness decision. Simply replacing vest_bal==0 with now>=deposit_hold_until would reintroduce historical reward dilution; clearing a completed marker does not fix the pre-expiry cycle. No safe minimal diff is established here. A separate protected tranche or immediate allocation of qualifying post-hold sweeps needs accounting review across sweep_trader and every trade normalisation before promotion.

LEAD | program: shortwin-venue-state | function: read_base | bug_class: hardening-mint-type-unchecked | group_key: shortwin-venue-state | read_base | hardening-mint-type-unchecked
file: crates/shortwin-venue-state/src/mint.rs:169
title: The base mint reader omits account type checks.
code_smells: The reader accepts every length above 81 bytes and does not inspect the Token-2022 account type.
description: A future caller that skips mint identity checks can accept token-account bytes as mint supply; current callers use constrained keys.
source_argument: read_base checks only owner in {TOKEN_PROGRAM, TOKEN_2022_PROGRAM}, data.len() >= 82, and base_of. In contrast, mint::check rejects legacy lengths other than 82, length 355, nonzero extension padding, and account type other than Mint. The program's authoritative check_mint_safety uses StateWithExtensions<Mint>::unpack, which performs the structural checks. A 166-byte buffer with valid base COption tags, byte 45 = 1 and byte 165 = 2 passes read_base but fails the strict type check. This is a parser counterexample, not an attacker-created, Token-2022-owned account.
callers: programs/shortwin/src/venues/pump_amm.rs:419 lp_mint_supply calls read_base without an additional length or type check; venues/mod.rs:1091 mint_supply does the same. Raydium's lp_supply separately requires exactly 82 bytes. PumpSwap ties the LP key to pool.lp_mint, and the named mint is constrained elsewhere.
verification_gap: This pass found no way for an outsider to replace an accepted named mint or canonical LP mint with the counterexample. Current key constraints prevent the proposed substitution.
minimal_fix: Add mint account length, padding, and type checks to read_base without applying the extension allowlist or freeze-authority policy to LP mints.

LEAD | program: shortwin | function: parse | bug_class: hardening-vault-authority-unchecked | group_key: shortwin | parse | hardening-vault-authority-unchecked
file: programs/shortwin/src/venues/raydium_v4.rs:146; programs/shortwin/src/venues/raydium_cpmm.rs:169
title: The Raydium state readers omit vault authority checks.
code_smells: Both parsers validate vault keys, token-program owners, and mints but omit the token authorities that their candidate verifiers check.
description: A future venue change can leave the readers to report an executable pool with invalid vault authorities; this pass found no current authority-change path.
source_argument: raydium_v4::parse accepts coin and pc when token_of succeeds and their mints match the pool. raydium_cpmm::parse does the same for v0 and v1. Their verify functions additionally require t.owner == the constant venue authority. read_state subsequently calls parse and state_of without that requirement. PumpSwap's vault_of performs the authority comparison on each read. These are separate loaders with different validation strength.
verification_gap: The recorded vault keys were checked at adoption. This pass did not prove that the deployed venues expose a way to change those vault authorities. A venue CPI would also reject an invalid authority rather than authorize token theft.
minimal_fix: Require both decoded vault token authorities to equal the corresponding Raydium authority inside each parse function.

LEAD | program: shortwin | function: math_tiers | bug_class: unbounded-tier-allocation | group_key: shortwin | math_tiers | unbounded-tier-allocation
file: programs/shortwin/src/venues/pump_curve.rs:404; programs/shortwin/src/venues/pump_amm.rs:608
title: The adapters copy each fee tier into the program heap.
code_smells: The shared fee reader bounds tier vectors by account length, while both adapters collect every tier into a Vec without a local count limit.
description: A fee-config expansion can exhaust the program heap before a reader returns no route; this pass did not prove a reachable failing tier count.
source_argument: pump::tiers_at checks offset arithmetic and slice bounds but no tier-count ceiling. pump_curve::pricing_inputs collects the curve tiers and uses Rc::from(math_tiers(pfc.fee_tiers)) for the pool tiers. pump_amm::read_state also collects its whole tier vector. open_short reads venue state before its prologue and again after its sell. The linked solana-program-entrypoint 3.1.1 defaults to HEAP_LENGTH = 32 * 1024, and BumpAllocator::dealloc is a no-op. Dropped vectors therefore do not restore heap space during the instruction. The documented 4097-byte FeeConfig allocation can structurally contain 100 forty-byte tiers plus both vector lengths and trailing fees, but that structural capacity does not prove the venue's setter permits that count.
verification_gap: No test or build ran. This pass did not establish the deployed fee-config setter's maximum tier count, the maximum allocation trace of an instruction, or a count that exhausts the heap. The current fixture schedules were not assessed as failing.
minimal_fix: Stream selection through the shared FeeTiers reader where possible and establish a measured bound for schedules retained by curve risk quotes.

LEAD | program: shortwin | function: elf_fingerprint_of | bug_class: hardening-truncated-elf-digest | group_key: shortwin | elf_fingerprint_of | hardening-truncated-elf-digest
file: programs/shortwin/src/state/venue_guard.rs:48
title: The upgrade latch stores only twelve bytes of each hash.
code_smells: The guard stores 12 of 32 SHA-256 bytes and compares only that prefix after an extension.
description: A venue authority can bypass the latch with paired ELF hashes that share twelve bytes; this pass found no such collision.
source_argument: GUARD_ELF_LEN = 12; elf_fingerprint_of copies only that prefix; VenueGuard.guard_elf holds four 12-byte arrays. flag_venue_upgraded::is_upgrade treats a changed ProgramData length as unchanged code when the new trimmed hash has the stored prefix. Thus an authority that controls two candidate ELFs can search a 96-bit collision before the first review, then combine the second upgrade with a later extension. A chosen pair has the generic birthday scale of 2^48 hashes, whereas replacing a fixed reviewed ELF has the much larger 2^96 second-preimage scale. Neither is an actual collision proof.
verification_gap: No colliding executable pair, practical work estimate, or deployed bypass was demonstrated. This is a hardening lead only. The source identifies AIR2-07 as an unresolved full-digest migration; that disclosure does not establish closure.
minimal_fix: Store and compare the full SHA-256 digest through an explicit account-layout migration.

LEAD | program: shortwin | function: exit_risk_cap_bps | bug_class: live-supply-risk-fee | group_key: shortwin | exit_risk_cap_bps | live-supply-risk-fee
file: programs/shortwin/src/venues/mod.rs:822; programs/shortwin/src/venues/pump_amm.rs:702
title: A supply burn can raise the PumpSwap risk fee.
code_smells: PumpSwap resolves both its live and EMA fee tiers from the current mint supply; the EMA price does not fix the supply input.
description: A holder can burn tokens before liquidation and raise its risk fee; this pass did not prove a profitable liquidation.
source_argument: pump_amm::read_state sets PammFeeSchedule.base_supply to its supplied live mint supply. It resolves fee_ema using quote = floor(P_ema * base / WAD) and that same schedule. PoolVenue.fee_ppm_at_ema feeds exit_risk_cap_bps, which limits risk quotes to min(hard_cap_bps, ceil(fee_ppm_at_ema / 100)). A burn lowers supply and market cap without changing P_ema, so a decreasing fee schedule can raise this cap. The source's exit_risk_cap_bps comment explicitly retains the burn residual as KI-72. The exposure is current for multi-tier PumpSwap schedules; the description does not assert an unexamined size or profit bound.
verification_gap: This pass did not construct or execute a concrete healthy position, burn, liquidation, and net-profit trace. The existing disclosure and its referenced test were located but were not treated as an independent reproduced proof.
minimal_fix: Resolve the risk-view fee from a supply value fixed before the current observation interval while execution quotes retain the live supply.
known_status: Source-disclosed KI-72; retained as a current source-supported lead, not closed by disclosure.

LEAD | program: shortwin | function: pricing_inputs | bug_class: live-supply-synthetic-risk-fee | group_key: shortwin | pricing_inputs | live-supply-synthetic-risk-fee
file: programs/shortwin/src/venues/pump_curve.rs:470
title: A burn can raise the curve's synthetic risk fee.
code_smells: The live curve's synthetic fee reads the current mint supply, and curve risk quotes retain it under the position's hard cap.
description: A holder can raise the synthetic risk fee after a burn under multiple tiers; this pass did not prove a liquidation.
source_argument: pricing_inputs resolves synthetic_fees with fees::pump_curve_at_supply(live.vt, live.vq, s, &schedule), where s is the live mint supply. CurvePricingInputs::curve_pricing forwards that value into CurvePricing.synthetic. Quoter::capped caps the resulting pricing at the position's cap but does not fix the market-cap supply. Quoter::buy_live and buy_xy use the synthetic route past rT. A supply burn can therefore change the fee used on the live and hypothetical risk paths in the same transaction under a multi-tier curve schedule. This differs from PumpSwap's exit cap and is not closed by its EMA cap.
verification_gap: The code documents a single flat curve tier in the pinned venue configuration, so this effect requires a fee-schedule change. This pass did not construct a liquidation at a tier boundary or measure a profitable burn.
minimal_fix: Resolve synthetic risk fees from a supply value fixed before the current observation interval while execution pricing follows the live supply.

A keeper restart clears the process-local cache. The recipient is externally configured, so this is not evidence of an arbitrary unauthenticated caller's ability to close it. The external token-account authority/close-authority state and production operational recovery were not verified. The implementation that owns the cache, keeper.rs, is outside the frozen source bundle; retain as a context-supported lead, not an in-scope finding.
missing_proof: Establish that a selected recipient can and does close the required ATA without changing the key, and inspect deployed operational recovery before judging practical severity.
minimal_fix_candidate: Invalidate pamm_ready after account-validation failures, or periodically recheck the accounts before relying on cached readiness.
